payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle claim. The cell’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. Projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. Its operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
